name: Nikolaos Papanikolopoulos
title: Professor; McKnight Presidential Endowed Professor; Minnesota Robotics Institute Director
department: Computer Science and Engineering; Minnesota Robotics Institute
researchAreas: Generative latent representations for robot control
fitReason: Strong CS-methods overlap through generative models that map human arm motion into executable robot configurations. A narrowly scoped representation-learning, motion-retargeting or evaluation component is an imaginable short project, subject to the host selecting a feasible task.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full February 2025 primary paper From Human Hands to Robotic Limbs implements a GRU-VAE plus feed-forward mapping on a physical Kinova Gen3 seven-DOF arm using Xsens Awinda motion tracking. Section III describes real-arm trajectory collection; Section IV reports four participants teleoperating the arm to three target poses, five trials each. This is learned human-motion teleoperation, not autonomous task planning or an LLM-controlled robot. Training human-motion data came from one person, a stated limitation.
